sentences: The bill would expand Airservices Australia’s duties concerning aircraft noise, community consultation and residential amenity, and establish independent complaint oversight and community representation arrangements.
A Melbourne flight plan would restrict helicopters and fixed-wing aircraft below 2,000 metres above sea level within five kilometres of the city centre.
The Melbourne restrictions would allow emergency, defence, hospital and other public interest exemptions, while the bill’s provisions would commence on the day of Royal Assent.
changes: Airservices Australia would have to establish community consultation groups and publish consultation details.
Its board could gain up to two members, including environmental management expertise and affected community representation.
New or changed flight paths made from 1 January 2012 could be reviewed on request.
Complaints handling and information exchanges with the ombudsman would require comprehensive reporting.
An independent Aircraft Noise Ombudsman would review complaints, and a Community Aviation Advocate would represent affected communities in consultations.
summary.affected: Airservices Australia, communities affected by aircraft noise and aircraft operators are affected.

speeches.speaker: Adam Bandt
speeches.brief: The Air Services Amendment Bill 2016 was introduced to strengthen community representation and protection from aircraft noise, requiring Airservices Australia to consult residents, appoint an independent Community Aviation Advocate and Aircraft Noise Ombudsman, add environmental and community representatives to its board, and ban helicopters and fixed-wing aircraft below 2,000 metres within five kilometres of central Melbourne.
